report.summary: The observable failure is confined to the recommendation call path. Between 00:42:40 and 00:43:57 the frontend's oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations client spans fail with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and the exact message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ETIMEDOUT 10.96.149.72:8080', the parent GET /api/recommendations spans return HTTP 500 after 74-125 s, and frontend-proxy/load-generator GET spans end in 504 after ~15.0 s; Loki shows the load generator's only failing endpoint is /api/recommendations. 10.96.149.72:8080 is the ClusterIP and port of Service recommendation; its single ready endpoint is pod recommendation-85cf7df656-c7v94 (10.244.234.145) on node sregym-worker. That pod is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, declares RECOMMENDATION_PORT/containerPort 8080 and logged 'listening on port 8080' at 00:42:11, yet a Loki query for the recommendation pods shows the newest 'Receive ListRecommendations' lines coming from its predecessor recommendation-6b9dd6f6fc-vflrj on the same node at 00:42:24-00:42:33 and only the startup line for c7v94. The recommendation Deployment's revision-2 and revision-3 ReplicaSet templates are identical (same image, port, nodeSelector); revision 3 only adds kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, i.e. the pod was replaced with an unchanged template. service:
  extensions: [jaeger_storage, jaeger_query, healthcheckv2]
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [jaeger_storage_exporter]
  telemetry:
    resource:
      service.name: jaeger
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
        - periodic:
            interval: 10000
            timeout: 5000
            exporter:
              otlp:
                protocol: http/protobuf
                endpoint: http://${env:OTEL_COLLECTOR_HOST}:${env:OTEL_COLLECTOR_PORT_HTTP}
                insecure: true
    logs:
      level: info
extensions:
  healthcheckv2:
    use_v2: true
    http:
      endpoint: 0.0.0.0:13133
  jaeger_query:
    storage:
      traces: memory_backend
      metrics: metrics_backend
    base_path: /jaeger/ui
  jaeger_storage:
    backends:
      memory_backend:
        memory:
          max_traces: ${env:MEMORY_MAX_TRACES}
    metric_backends:
      metrics_backend:
        prometheus:
          endpoint: "http://${env:PROMETHEUS_ADDR}"
          normalize_calls: true
          normalize_duration: true

receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:JAEGER_HOST}:${env:JAEGER_GRPC_PORT}

processors:
  batch:

exporters:
  jaeger_storage_exporter:
    trace_storage: memory_backend

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
